Memorandum To: Review committees From: Jean S.
VanderGheynst, Dean, College of the Environment and Life Sciences Re: Proposal to merge Department of Landscape Architecture and Department of Geosciences Date: November 7, 2025 ————————————————————————————————————— I fully support the proposed merger of the Department of Landscape Architecture (LAR) and the Department of Geosciences (GEO).
This merger aligns with the University’s strategic goals to strengthen interdisciplinary collaboration, enhance program sustainability, and advance our land and sea grant mission.
A budget and justification summarizing how existing resources will be used is included in the submission.
The Department of Landscape Architecture offers Rhode Island’s only accredited undergraduate program of its kind and is approaching re-accreditation in 2026.
The upcoming retirement of its two tenured faculty members would leave the program without tenured or tenure-track faculty, jeopardizing accreditation.
To ensure continuity and demonstrate institutional commitment, two tenure-track faculty searches focused on Environmental Planning and Urban Design and Transportation Planning have been approved.

The merger with Geosciences, which includes several tenured and tenure-track faculty, provides the necessary structure to support new hires and ensure compliance with Article 15 of the collective bargaining agreement.
Both departments have voted in favor of the merger, recognizing the intellectual and operational benefits of joining two small, synergistic units.
Together, they will form a hub addressing climate change, resilience planning, sustainable development, and management of natural resources.
The merged department will enhance shared teaching, research, and outreach capacity while maintaining all existing academic programs without disruption or impact on other departments or colleges.
This merger represents a forward-looking investment in programs that exemplify URI’s strengths in environmental and community-based problem solving.
It supports the continued accreditation of the Bachelor of Landscape Architecture program and positions URI as a regional leader in sustainable design and Earth system science.

Curricular Matters Which Require Confirmation By The Faculty Senate COURSE CHANGES COLLEGE OF ARTS & SCIENCES: ART 354 | Art of the Ancient Mediterranean, Effective Fall 2025 Eliminate prerequisites (3 crs.) Developments in architecture, painting, and sculpture in Greece and Rome from 800 B.C. to 400 A.D. Brief analysis of the art of the Aegean from 2500 to 1500 B.C. (Lec. 3) May be repeated once with permission of instructor. ART 356 | Medieval Art, Effective Spring 2026 Eliminate prerequisites (3 crs.) Painting, sculpture, architecture, and minor arts of the Middle Ages from 500 to 1400 in Western Europe. (Lec. 3) ART 361 | Modern Art, Effective Winter 2025 Eliminate prerequisites (3 crs.) Investigates major movements of European and American painting, sculpture, printmaking, and photography from the late nineteenth to the mid-twentieth century. (Lec. 3/Online) ART 364 | American Art, Effective Fall 2025 Eliminate prerequisites (3 crs.) Painting, sculpture, and architecture from their origins in the 17th century to the present; emphasis on the 19th century. (Lec. 3) ART 385 | Women in Art, Effective Spring 2026 Eliminate prerequisites (3 crs.) Examination of women artists and their work in the history of western art; analysis of representations of women and gender in works of art and art historical texts. (Lec. 3)

CHM 112 | General Chemistry Lecture II, Effective Summer 2025 Change prerequisites (3 crs.) Chemical kinetics, equilibrium, elementary thermodynamics and electrochemistry integrated with descriptive chemistry and practical applications. (Lec. 3) Pre: CHM 101 with a grade of C- or better, or CHM 103 with a grade of B or better.
CHM 114 | Laboratory for Chemistry 112, Effective Summer 2025 Change prerequisites (1 cr.) Experiments follow the content of CHM 112. (Lab. 2) Pre: Credit or concurrent enrollment in CHM 112, and CHM 102 or CHM 105 with a grade of B or better.
The above mentioned CHM112 and CHM114 were pulled from the floor of the Faculty Senate Meeting regarding concerns of the prerequisite changes.
CSF 432 | Introduction to Network and Systems Security, Effective Fall 2025 Change prerequisites (4 crs.) This course provides an overview of network and systems security.
It provides the underlying theory of computer security.
It further introduces hands-on skills and techniques that are essential to effectively secure the networks and systems of large and small organizations. (Online) Pre: Minimum cumulative GPA of 2.7 and B or better in CSF 202, or by permission of instructor.

STA 400 | Introduction to the Analysis of Missing Data, Effective Fall 2025 Change prerequisites (4 crs.) Upper-level undergraduate course in missing data analysis.
Covered topics will include missing data methods in experiments, deletion methods, single imputation methods, and multiple imputations. (Lec. 3, Lab. 1) Pre: STA 307 or STA308, and STA 411 or STA 412, or by permission of the instructor.
Not for graduate credit.
COLLEGE OF EDUCATION: EDC 308 | Supervised Experience in Health Education, Effective Fall 2025 Change credit hours, prerequisites (3 cr.) Students participate in supervised experience laboratory for methods learned in EDC 307: Methods of School Health Instruction; (Practicum).
Pre: concurrent enrollment in EDC 307, admission to the College of Education or Admission to the Master of Education program or permission of the instructor.

EDC 315 | Supervised Experience-Physical Education in Secondary School, Effective Fall 2025 Change credit hours (3 cr.) Students participate in supervised experience laboratory for methods learned in 314. (Practicum) Pre: Concurrent enrollment in EDC 314, admission to the College of Education or Admission to the Master of Education program or permission of the instructor.

Analyze learning and studying in college settings; Assess college learning needs, apply effective study and work management strategies to academics, and improve metacognitive awareness and academic skills. (Seminar/Online) Pre: permission of instructor.

Development of skills and knowledge necessary to make educational and career decisions; utilize self- assessment inventories to identify aptitudes, values, and interests as they relate to majors and careers. (Seminar/Online) Pre: Not for students with more than 75 credits.

(Lec. 3/Online) Pre: PSY 113.
Open to Kinesiology majors only, or permission of instructor.
NUT 210 | General Nutrition Lab, Effective Fall 2025 Change title and update prerequisites (1 cr.) Weekly laboratory experience collecting and interpreting dietary intake, anthropometric measures, and clinical values. (Lab. 2) Pre: Credit or concurrent enrollment in NUT 207.

Landscape Architecture Landscape architecture is a 126-credit curriculum leading to the Bachelor of Landscape Architecture (B.L.A.) degree.
Accredited by the Landscape Architecture Accreditation Board of the ASLA, the curriculum is designed to prepare undergraduates for professional careers in public and private practice.
Landscape architecture is a profession that involves the design, planning, preservation, and restoration of the landscape by applying art, science, and technology to achieve the best use of our land and water resources.
Landscape architects design and plan parks, plazas, and recreation areas; residential, institutional and commercial developments; transportation facilities, new towns and campus landscapes, and green infrastructure.
They are also involved in planning and designing landscapes in coastal areas and inland developments impacted by climate.
The requirements of this curriculum include preparation in the basic arts and sciences.

The major includes 63-64 credits of professional core classes (LAR 101, 201, 202, 243, 244, 300, 301, 302, 343, 344, 345, 346, 353, 354, 443, 444, 445, 447, 450); 28-29 credits of supporting requirements (ART 207; GEG 101; PLS 150; CHM 100, 101 or 103 or PHY 109, or GEO 100G, or 103; CPL 410, CPL 434, 538; MTH 103; and PLS 200); and 7-8 credits of supporting electives.
Students will also take general education classes and 6-7 credits of free electives.
Students accepted into landscape architecture are required to maintain a grade point average of at least 2.50 with no landscape architecture grades below a letter C.
